reviewer.name: Codex coordinator with three independent read-only scopes

snapshot.workingTree: Specification/proof sources unchanged; existing audit work preserved. Both proof packages are machine-local outside this repository Git tree.

included: All current41 Lean chapters plus root and23 EasyCrypt sources for fresh validity
Source-first semantic review of new trial proofs and dependencies
Same generation/source/refusal/budgets, exact2^-120, loop law and both-system correspondence
All supplied documentation/review claims and exact proposed timing changes
excluded: Sequential first-success rule only; general2^-136*n, workers and capped generation exposing attempts are not final formal endpoints.
Finite full passphrase alphabet, independent priors/functions, idealized cryptography, total-program/losslessness classes and hard budgets retain the development's stated scope.
The2^-120 addend is verified, not claimed optimal; Lean need not state the sharper strict variance/deviation formula used in the prose or EC proof.
Lean finite prefixes/survival/capped_close characterize the unbounded law on nonempty passing sets; no separate named Tendsto/uniqueness theorem is declared.
Empty passing sets use exceptional completion/nontermination conventions; their mass is included in bounds, not asserted to terminate physically.
No implementation clock, PBKDF2 timing, OS scheduler, random-generator/runtime cost, native Rust/WASM/CLI/browser or concrete cryptographic primitive audit.
Dependencies reused at13 pinned clean Git revisions; no clean install/cache download, release artifact, full-cost Argon2/vector execution or remote CI.
Two initial KnownPair strict SMT failures were preserved; final successful run used more available CPU/memory. No proof, assertion, timeout or solver configuration was weakened.
Prior review hashes are historical: current Lean TrialCount and EC TrialCount differ from its first hash table; this audit uses its own exact snapshot and fresh checks.
Specification and proof sources were not edited; wording is proposed only, with no commit or push.

findings.title: The general disclosed-trials claim needs explicit secret-independent selection and scheduling coins
findings.blockingReason: Blocks the unrestricted literal general-rule disclosure claim. It does not block the correctly scoped sequential formal result; an explicit independence qualification resolves the gap.
findings.affected: Specification DESIGN-NOTES.md:4703-4712 and4738-4761, specifically applying the first three selection conditions to the disclosed-trials extension.
findings.reproduction: Take a uniform binary password P and a singleton passphrase alphabet. Let C be the fair bit identifying P, independent of the iid entropy draws and the random functions. Stop at the first passing draw when C=0 and the second passing draw when C=1. Under the literal stated independence condition C is independent of trial values, and the rule uses only order/outcomes/C and terminates almost surely on nonempty U.
findings.expected: The ideal disclosed transcript can be simulated independently of the secrets/functions. Selection/scheduling randomness for a disclosed-trial rule must be jointly sampled independently of secrets, functions and underlying entropy draws, with no extra hidden inputs to the policy.
findings.observed: The selected entropy is uniform on U for either password, so hidden-trial source equivalence survives. But the disclosed number of PASS outcomes is one or two and identifies P. The pair attacker uses no oracle queries. On successful generation it wins with probability1 rather than approximately1/2; the ideal expected count is1.5*2^16, so the proposed2^-136*n addition remains tiny. Empty-U exceptional mass does not remove that gap.
findings.impact: The broad general-rule sentence is not valid under its literal marginal-independence reading. Conventional fresh private coins exclude this countermodel, but that stronger intended hypothesis needs to be explicit. No checked Lean/EasyCrypt sequential theorem permits this policy or is refuted by it, and no implementation leak is alleged.
findings.evidence: Independent wording scope proposed the missing hypothesis; an independent Lean scope challenged and confirmed the first-versus-second-pass countermodel, including the empty-U qualification. The original selection clause only names independence from trial values, while the timing clause names secrets/functions too. Detailed argument in annexes.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the explicit fresh joint-independence condition to A.6's number-of-trials disclosure paragraph. Keep the earlier hidden-trial selection rule separate: it need not be strengthened merely to support this extension. Retain the sequential/general/workers formal-coverage distinctions.
findings.requiredVerification: The revised statement excludes the P-correlated selection bit, permits independent randomized scheduling, and does not demand conditional independence after observing stopping/outcomes. Preserve all sequential endpoint hypotheses and constants. No general-worker formal theorem should be claimed until proved.

findings.title: Timing summaries do not consistently state the permitted postprocessing condition
findings.affected: Specification README.md:805-806; DESIGN-NOTES.md:506-508,3963-3965 consistency; EasyCrypt README.md:114-115.
findings.reproduction: Read the elapsed-time permission literally: delaying each trial by an encoding of the MHFE password depends neither on the trial value nor the passphrase, yet reveals the password. Compare with A.6's stricter outcomes-plus-independent-coins condition.
findings.expected: Timing is a common postprocessing of the allowed outcome/count transcript and randomness jointly independent of secrets, functions and trial values, at fixed public settings. It has no additional hidden dependence.
findings.observed: The specification README excludes only trial value and passphrase, leaving password/function dependence unexcluded. The two DESIGN-NOTES phrases saying only on these are narrower deterministic shorthands, not independent unsafe permissions; adding independent coins makes them consistent. The EasyCrypt README names only secret-independence rather than the full list.
findings.impact: A reader can overestimate which timer is covered. The actual sequential formal interfaces support the stricter A.6 condition, and real hardware/BIP39/OS timing has not been proved to satisfy it. This is a wording mismatch, not a false checked bound or evidence of an implemented timing attack.
findings.evidence: Three source-first scopes agree on the README counterexample and shared-kernel interpretation. Lean samples a strategy PMF outside the whole generation; EC exposes only the actual outcomes and the adversary's own coins under its global restrictions.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the three proposed specification replacements in PROPOSED-WORDING.md, and align the EasyCrypt README or link to the central condition. Say no additional dependence rather than unconditional independence of the duration itself, since the allowed outcomes already depend on S/T/Q.
findings.requiredVerification: All summaries agree with A.6, allow outcome-derived duration plus independent noise, exclude the password-delay witness, and do not claim that arbitrary measured wall-clock time or capped-and-revealed generation has been verified.
